turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training samples with the highest measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (all \(>1080\) MPa, up to 1144 MPa) belong exclusively to the carburized subset (NT = CT = 930 °C, DT \(\approx 850{-}900\) °C, TT = 160 or 200 °C). All other heat-treatment families in the training data peak at \(\le 906\) MPa. Consequently only the 11 carburized candidates in the pool can possibly occupy the top ranks.

Nearest-neighbour matching plus the observed effects of the two most influential process variables (TT and Ct) yields the following approximate strengths:

- c081 matches the single strongest training composition (Cr = 1.17, RedRatio = 690) except for a 40 °C rise in TT; the typical TT penalty in this family is only 20–40 MPa, leaving a prediction \(\approx 1100\) MPa.
- c053 matches the second-strongest training composition (Ni = 1.69, RedRatio = 860) except for a shorter Ct and a more favourable TT; the two changes largely cancel, again giving \(\approx 1100\) MPa.
- c063 and c062 are exact process/composition swaps of the 1082 MPa and 1034 MPa training points (both TT = 160 °C), producing predictions in the 1050–1070 MPa range.
- c046 realises the 1089 MPa process window (TT = 160 °C) with a closely related Cr–Mo chemistry, giving \(\approx 1050\) MPa.

All remaining carburized candidates are either higher-TT or lower-RedRatio analogues and fall 30–80 MPa lower. The five candidates above are therefore the clear top rank.

Final: c081, c053, c063, c062, c046
